questions.question:
Identify the sentence that correctly uses inversion to emphasize the adverbial phrase.

A. Never before have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
B. Only after the storm passed did the sun reappear.
C. So fast did the car go that it almost crashed.
D. Hardly had I arrived when the meeting started.
options: Never before have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
Only after the storm passed did the sun reappear.
So fast did the car go that it almost crashed.
Hardly had I arrived when the meeting started.
questions.answer: Only after the storm passed did the sun reappear.

questions.question:
Which of the following sentences correctly employs a cleft sentence to highlight the specific detail about the event?

A. It was John who called the meeting yesterday.
B. That John called the meeting yesterday was unexpected.
C. John called the meeting yesterday, which was unexpected.
D. Yesterday, John was the one who called the meeting.
options: It was John who called the meeting yesterday.
That John called the meeting yesterday was unexpected.
John called the meeting yesterday, which was unexpected.
Yesterday, John was the one who called the meeting.
questions.answer: It was John who called the meeting yesterday.

questions.question:
Select the option that correctly uses the subjunctive mood to express a hypothetical condition.

A. If I were you, I would accept the offer.
B. If I was you, I would accept the offer.
C. If I had been you, I would have accepted the offer.
D. If I had been you, I would accept the offer.
options: If I were you, I would accept the offer.
If I was you, I would accept the offer.
If I had been you, I would have accepted the offer.
If I had been you, I would accept the offer.
questions.answer: If I were you, I would accept the offer.

questions.question:
Which sentence correctly uses ellipsis to maintain grammatical parallelism and meaning?

A. She likes reading books, swimming in the sea, and hiking in the mountains.
B. She likes reading books, to swim in the sea, and hiking in the mountains.
C. She likes to read books, swimming in the sea, and to hike in the mountains.
D. She likes reading books, to swim in the sea, and hiking in the mountains.
options: She likes reading books, swimming in the sea, and hiking in the mountains.
She likes reading books, to swim in the sea, and hiking in the mountains.
She likes to read books, swimming in the sea, and to hike in the mountains.
She likes reading books, to swim in the sea, and hiking in the mountains.
questions.answer: She likes reading books, swimming in the sea, and hiking in the mountains.

questions.question:
Choose the sentence that appropriately uses formal register and complex sentence structure to convey a nuanced grammatical choice.

A. If the committee had been aware of the situation, they would have acted differently.
B. If the committee was aware of the situation, they would have acted differently.
C. The committee should have acted differently if they were aware of the situation.
D. The committee would have acted differently if they were aware of the situation.
options: If the committee had been aware of the situation, they would have acted differently.
If the committee was aware of the situation, they would have acted differently.
The committee should have acted differently if they were aware of the situation.
The committee would have acted differently if they were aware of the situation.
questions.answer: If the committee had been aware of the situation, they would have acted differently.
